valuation.net_debt_note: EV = market cap + latest borrowings. Screener's public page does not split cash out of other assets, so cash is not netted off; investments are shown separately.

dcf.method: 5-year FCFF: EBITDA - tax on EBIT - capex - change in net working capital; growth fades linearly from the starting rate to the year-5 rate; Gordon terminal value; equity = EV - borrowings.

inputs.growth_basis: median of 3-year, 5-year and TTM sales growth, capped 0-30%
inputs.capex_rule: depreciation + new sales / fixed-asset turnover (median of the last three years)

reverse_dcf.note: Constant sales growth for five years, at the base margin and the same WACC and terminal growth, that makes the DCF equal today's EV.

blocks.text: [F] Hexagon Nutrition makes and sells nutrition products in three revenue lines: branded clinical and wellness nutrition (PentaSure, PediaGold, Obesigo, Nutrone), customised vitamin-mineral premixes sold to FMCG and pharma companies, and an 'ESG' line of therapeutic and humanitarian foods (RUTF, RUSF, micronutrient powders) sold largely through institutional and government tenders (AR2026 p.5) (PPT Aug 2026). [F] It reports a single operating segment, 'Nutraceuticals', and discloses revenue, but not profit, by product line (AR2026 p.124). [F] FY26 consolidated revenue from operations was Rs 382.6 cr, EBITDA Rs 52.9 cr and PAT Rs 37.9 cr (AR2026 p.56). [F] Our statements data shows FY26 sales of Rs 380 cr, EBITDA Rs 53 cr and PAT Rs 38 cr (NUMBERS).

[F] FY26 is the first audited year disclosed to public-market investors, Q1 FY27 is the first reported quarter, and the DRHP/RHP was not available to us. [AI] The public evidence base is therefore one annual report, two calls and one presentation: guidance has no track record and several operating metrics already conflict across documents.

blocks.text: [AI] Driver classification: thesis 1 (branded mix) is company-specific; thesis 2 (utilisation) is company-specific; thesis 3 (premix and fortification demand) is partly structural (fortification mandates) and partly company-specific (FMCG wallet share); thesis 4 (humanitarian tenders) is cyclical and policy-driven; thesis 5 (order book) is cyclical; thesis 6 (balance sheet) is company-specific.

items: 1. Valuation already discounts a different company. [F] Our DCF values the equity at Rs 17.7 per share (base) and Rs 27.4 (bull) against a price of Rs 68.8; the reverse DCF needs about 72% sales growth a year for five years against 10.9% in the base case (NUMBERS).

2. Cash conversion collapsed in FY26. [F] CFO was Rs 6 cr against PAT of Rs 38 cr (CFO/PAT 0.16) and FCF was negative Rs 1 cr (NUMBERS); [F] receivables rose Rs 23.1 cr and inventories Rs 22.7 cr (AR2026 p.98).
3. Working capital is structurally heavy. [F] Cash conversion cycle 179 days and inventory days 153 at FY26 (NUMBERS); [MC] inventory still about 142 days at Q1 FY27 (CALL Aug 2026).

4. Margin expansion reversed in the first listed quarter. [F] Q1 FY27 EBITDA margin was 11.3% vs 13.8% a year earlier, and gross margin fell about 3pt (PPT Aug 2026) (CALL Aug 2026); [MC] the recovery depends on 10-15% MRP increases and cost pass-through (CALL Aug 2026).

5. The IPO was entirely a promoter exit. [F] All 3.09 cr shares sold were existing shares at Rs 45 (AR2026 p.126); [E] the fall in promoter-group shares from about 10.99 cr before the IPO (AR2026 p.49) to 64.29% of the enlarged base (NUMBERS) matches the OFS size, implying that promoter-group holders sold almost all of the OFS shares.

6. Board instability right after listing. [F] Two promoter-family directors (Subhash and Aditya Kelkar) resigned on 6 July 2026 without disclosed reasons (AR2026 p.32); [F] the Chairman ceased on 28 September 2026 and shareholders requisitioned an EGM to re-appoint him (ANNOUNCEMENTS).

7. Promoter pay is large relative to profit. [F] KMP remuneration to five Kelkar family members was Rs 7.40 cr in FY26 (AR2026 p.120), about 19.5% of PAT [E]; [F] the AGM sought higher caps totalling Rs 6.23 cr for three of them (AR2026 p.27).

8. Disclosure quality is uneven. [F] The CARO report says monthly bank returns did not agree with the books (AR2026 p.60), while a note says they did (AR2026 p.92); the consolidated debt-service ratio is shown as 0.78 in the notes and 1.89 in the MD&A (AR2026 p.126) (AR2026 p.56).

9. The ESG line is lumpy and fell in FY26. [F] ESG revenue fell 16.5% to Rs 65.0 cr on 'delay in release of tenders' (AR2026 p.31); [F] Ethiopia alone was Rs 39.4 cr of FY25 revenue and was below the 10% threshold in FY26 (AR2026 p.124).

10. Two foreign subsidiaries carry going-concern doubts. [F] Other auditors flagged material uncertainty for the South Africa and Uzbekistan subsidiaries, which have combined net liabilities of Rs 12.2 cr (AR2026 p.93) (AR2026 p.125).

Is Q1 FY27's +43% growth a new run-rate or a soft base? [F] Q1 FY26 revenue was only Rs 72.9 cr, the weakest quarter shown (NUMBERS). [MC] Management guided only 20-25% for the year (CALL Aug 2026). [AI] Growth may look strong on a soft base yet still fall short of guidance in H2, where FY26 had large ESG dispatches.

Is FY26 margin improvement structural? [MC] Management attributes it to branded mix and premix volume (CALL Jul 2026). [F] Q1 FY27 margin fell back to 11.3% (PPT Aug 2026). [AI] The market may be extrapolating the FY26 peak; equally, the field-force and freight costs may prove temporary.

What is the order book really? [MC] 'Rs 100 crores' to be executed in Q2 and part of Q3 (CALL Aug 2026). [F] Neither the annual report nor the presentation discloses an order book. [AI] This is roughly one quarter of revenue, not multi-year visibility.

How much is the humanitarian franchise worth? [MC] Management describes UN approval as a barrier to entry (AR2026 p.5). [F] Yet ESG revenue fell in FY26 and was about 10% of Q1 FY27 revenue [MC] (CALL Aug 2026). The market may be over- or under-pricing an option on tender wins.

Is the stock cheap on earnings or expensive on cash? [F] Trailing P/E is 22.3x and EV/EBITDA 16.6x (NUMBERS), but FY26 FCF was negative [F] (NUMBERS). [AI] Investors focused on P/E may underweight the cash gap; investors focused on the DCF may underweight the high WACC (14.8%) built into our model [F] (NUMBERS).

blocks.text: [AI] The consensus narrative, judging by the questions on both calls, is a branded-nutrition growth story with 30-47% utilisation and operating leverage ahead. Our read is that the business is mostly a premix contract manufacturer (53% of revenue) with a growing but sub-scale B2C brand, a lumpy tender business, and a working-capital model that absorbed nearly all of FY26's profit. [F] At Rs 68.8 the price sits above our bull-case DCF value of Rs 27.4 (NUMBERS). [AI] For the shares to be supported on fundamentals, cash conversion has to normalise in FY27 and the gross-margin recovery promised for Q2 has to show up. The upside risk to this view is that the B2C line compounds at 20%+ with 60%+ gross margins for longer than a DCF with a 14.8% WACC credits.

blocks.text: [MC] Management's segment gross margins are branded 60-68%, premix 35-40% and ESG 25-30% (CALL Jul 2026). [E] Weighting midpoints of those ranges by FY26 mix (30/53/17) gives about 44%, close to the reported Q4 FY26 and Q1 FY27 gross margin of about 43.9% [E] (PPT Aug 2026). That suggests the stated ranges are broadly credible. [AI] Value is captured mainly in formulation know-how and the PentaSure brand, not in manufacturing scale; vitamin inputs are bought in, and premix customers can dual-source.

blocks.text: [AI] Standard premixes for staple fortification (flour, rice, oil) are the most commodity-like: specifications are set by regulators, and the global vitamin majors also supply them. Customised premixes for FMCG beverages and infant nutrition are stickier because they are embedded in the customer's product formulation. ESG products are differentiated by approval, not by product, and are priced through tenders. PentaSure is the only line with evidence of brand pull: an analyst reported that pharmacies recognise PentaSure but not PediaGold or Obesigo, and management did not dispute it [MC] (CALL Jul 2026).

Premix: [MC] a domestic premix 'order jump' dispatched in Q4 (CALL Jul 2026); [F] domestic +44.1%, export +24.9% (AR2026 p.31). [AI] Strongest line, but it includes order-timing effects and is the lowest-margin non-ESG line.
